question_text: I am very sorry _______ to attend the meeting yesterday.
explanation: The correct structure is 'sorry to have failed'.

question_text: When you are faced with an examination of this nature, endeavour to keep your mind _______ the job and not be distracted for one moment.
explanation: To keep your mind 'on' something means to focus on it.

question_text: The dull student took a correspondence course as a means _______ his standard in the class.
explanation: A 'means of improving' is the correct phrase.

question_text: The thief ran _______ luck when the policeman running after him caught up with him and knocked him down.
explanation: To 'run out of luck' means to stop being lucky.

question_text: Your brigade would be the better for it, if you desisted _______ rumor mongering, observed the Chief of Staff.
explanation: To 'desist from' something means to stop doing it.

question_text: He received a pat _______ the back for his brilliant success in the examination.
explanation: A 'pat on the back' is an idiom for praise or encouragement.

question_text: I am _______ to receive this week's holiday duty grant.
explanation: To be 'entitled to' something means to have a right to it.

question_text: A number of suspects were paraded _______ the victim of the robbery.
explanation: To be paraded 'before' someone means to be shown to them, often in an official capacity.

question_text: I was _______ hearing distance of the speaker.
explanation: To be 'within hearing distance' means to be close enough to hear.

question_text: Bassey's evidence _______ Okon being imprisoned for life.
explanation: 'Led to' indicates a cause-and-effect relationship.

question_text: The nurse kept apologizing to mothers as she stuck her needle _______ every baby at the clinic.
explanation: To stick a needle 'into' someone or something.

question_text: My brother does not have a flair _______ Mathematics.
explanation: A 'flair for' something means a natural talent for it.

question_text: The poor little kid has been down _______ few these few days.
explanation: To be 'down with' an illness means to be sick.

question_text: The villagers looked _______ their leader for good examples.
explanation: To 'look up to' someone means to respect them.

question_text: The _______ of the cliff after his shoes had failed to grip.
explanation: To 'fall off' something means to lose one's grip and drop down.

question_text: Wale Agun, in creating his characters, draws freely _______ his experience.
explanation: To 'draw on' experience means to use it as a resource.

question_text: There is no need to stand _______ ceremony in matters of this nature.
explanation: To stand 'on ceremony' means to insist on formal behavior.

question_text: I am not in a position to stand _______ such a huge sum of money.
explanation: To 'stand for' something in this context means to tolerate or bear the cost of it.

question_text: We cannot explain his objection _______ the new law.
explanation: An 'objection to' something is the correct phrase.

question_text: Silk materials ought to be prohibited _______ being brought into the country.
explanation: To be prohibited 'from' doing something.

question_text: The answers _______ the questions were discussed _______ the students.
explanation: The answer 'to' a question is discussed 'with' someone.

question_text: I can always depend _______ my father for my survival.
explanation: To 'depend on' someone means to rely on them.

question_text: The point _______ the story is that he is the man's son.
explanation: The 'point of' the story is the main idea.

question_text: The Director _______ is in charge to ensure the success of the programme.
explanation: The 'Director of' a programme is in charge.

question_text: I wanted to avail myself _______ the opportunity of listening to the lecture.
explanation: To 'avail oneself of' something means to take advantage of it.

question_text: Little Tunde realized that he was being made a fool _______
explanation: To be made a 'fool of' means to be tricked.

question_text: Mr and Mrs. Akiola were sad and disappointed _______ the performance of their son.
explanation: To be disappointed 'with' someone or something.

question_text: When the transformer blew up, Saka threw himself down _______ his stomach.
explanation: To lie 'on' one's stomach is the correct preposition.

question_text: A programme of good exercise may help a person fight _______ cold.
explanation: To 'fight off' a cold means to resist or overcome it.

question_text: Adabi is contemptuous _______
explanation: To be contemptuous 'of' or 'for' something.

question_text: My goats are grazing _______ a field.
explanation: To graze 'in' a field.

question_text: You avoid facing _______ reality.
explanation: To 'face up to' reality means to accept it.

question_text: The policemen who were to keep watch connived _______ a thief.
explanation: To 'connive with' someone means to secretly cooperate with them.

question_text: The secretary was blamed _______ the untidy state of the office.
explanation: To be blamed 'for' something.

question_text: Idubor has gone to see his mechanic because his car engine needs to be tuned _______.
explanation: To 'tune up' an engine means to adjust it for better performance.

question_text: The patient was _______ by a group of surgeons last week.
explanation: The correct structure is 'operated on' (the patient).

question_text: Until his recent experience, Onimisi used to pride himself _______ his fearlessness.
explanation: To 'pride oneself on' something is correct.

question_text: The director is liable _______ what his accountants do.
explanation: To be liable 'for' something means to be responsible for it.

question_text: Some motorists _______ to push their cars to the nearest filling station.
explanation: The correct phrase is 'have to push'.

question_text: The workers suffered a lot, toiling _______ the sun.
explanation: To toil 'in' the sun is correct.

question_text: He was angry _______ me for not allowing him to use my pen.
explanation: To be angry 'with' a person is correct.

question_text: She has been here _______ five minutes.
explanation: 'For' is used with a duration of time.

question_text: The driver of the car admitted _______ to not having a licence.
explanation: To admit 'to not having' a licence is the correct gerund phrase.

question_text: The hospital _______ closed, because there were no beds to put patients _______
explanation: 'The hospital is closed up' and 'beds to put patients in'.

question_text: Students were forbidden _______ from joining in the demonstration.
explanation: To be forbidden 'from' doing something.

question_text: All the traders in the market saw the woman buy _______ a fool.
explanation: To buy something 'as' a fool means to buy it foolishly.

question_text: The girl says she is averse _______ what others admire.
explanation: To be averse 'to' something means to dislike it.

question_text: The members of the other team agree _______ all the terms of the contract.
explanation: To agree 'with' terms or a person is the standard structure.

question_text: He is _______ Kaduna.
explanation: 'In' is used for cities and large towns.

question_text: _______ Owning to B. Due to C. Referring D. With reference to official assignment.
explanation: The correct formal phrase is 'With reference to'.

question_text: Although he was sorry _______ his illness, Muhammed could not find someone to do his work.
explanation: To be sorry 'about' something.

question_text: _______ I was angry.
explanation: 'Owing to' means because of.

question_text: The man is refurbishing the house with a view to _______.
explanation: The phrase 'with a view to' is followed by a gerund (verb + ing).

question_text: As we sat _______ the silence, my eyes _______ A. in/roamed B. under/roamed C. on/roamed D. at/roamed
explanation: We sit 'in' silence. The correct option is A.

question_text: The money was shared _______ the five brothers.
explanation: 'Among' is used for more than two people.

question_text: She refrained _______ smoking.
explanation: To refrain 'from' doing something is correct.

question_text: Judging _______ his face, he is not guilty.
explanation: To judge 'by' appearance is correct.

question_text: If you want to succeed in life, don't be envious _______ other people's achievement.
explanation: To be envious 'of' someone is correct.

question_text: They are taught to value honesty _______.
explanation: To value something 'above' all else.

question_text: Our plan for the trip fell _______ when the rich man did not give us a life.
explanation: To 'fall through' means to fail to happen.

question_text: I tried to dissuade him, but he persisted _______ revealing the secret to his son.
explanation: To persist 'in' doing something.

question_text: He can recall the important dates in the nation's history, it is interesting to listen to him as he rattles _______ A. up
correct: To rattle 'off' means to say something quickly.

question_text: His wife was badly injured in the fracas, but I think she will pull _______.
explanation: To 'pull through' means to recover from a serious illness or injury.

question_text: The principal said that he was pleased _______ my effort.
explanation: To be pleased 'with' something is correct.

question_text: Paper is made _______ woodpulp.
explanation: Paper is made 'from' woodpulp (the raw material is changed).

question_text: The policeman was sent _______ exile.
explanation: To send someone 'into' exile is the correct phrase.

question_text: _______ is still spread _______ word of mouth in most villages in Africa.
explanation: Information spreads 'through' word of mouth.

question_text: He was both a writer and a politician, but he was better _______.
explanation: He was better 'as a' writer.

question_text: She was _______ the verge of tears.
explanation: 'On the verge of' is the correct idiom.

question_text: _______ your parents' room, we shouldn't see each other anymore.
explanation: 'As for' means regarding or concerning.

question_text: The chairman is too much _______ an idealist for this government.
explanation: 'Too much of an idealist' is the correct structure.

question_text: What is the jury's _______ the matter?
explanation: The 'verdict on' a matter is the correct phrase.

question_text: She traced her family history _______ maternal descent.
explanation: To trace history 'from' an origin.

question_text: The philanthropist devote himself _______ the poor.
explanation: To devote oneself 'to doing' something is correct.

question_text: The police described the boy as being _______ hand.
explanation: To be 'on hand' means to be present or available.

question_text: We have a family mutiny... our hands.
explanation: To have something 'on' one's hands.

question_text: The number of stores will be _______ twenty to thirty.
explanation: 'From twenty to thirty' indicates a range.

question_text: The company deals _______ computer software.
explanation: To deal 'in' a product means to trade it.

question_text: They are taught to value honesty _______ all else.
explanation: To value something 'above' all else.

question_text: He can recall the important dates in the nation's history, it is interesting to listen to him as he rattles _______
explanation: To rattle 'off' means to say something quickly.
